## Method Overview

<!-- Learn muscle synergies from one person's walking, then make the RL policy control *synergies* instead of individual muscles. -->
> *Can embedding neurophysiological structure (muscle synergies) into RL improve the biomechanical fidelity of predictive simulation?* [@park2026synergy]

::: {.horiz style="align-items: stretch;"}
::: {style="flex: 1; font-size: 0.75em;" .box}
**1. Record real-world walking.**

- 1 person with motion capture and force plates.
- Extract 10 strides from clip.

$\rightarrow$ *Task-space markers & ground reaction forces (GRF).*
:::

::: {.flow-arrow}
→
:::

::: {style="flex: 1; font-size: 0.75em;" .box}
**2. Estimate muscle activity**

- Build MSM (H2190) with subject anatomy.
- Inverse kinematics to compute joint angles.
- Subject to kinematic and GRF constraints, find valid muscle activations that consume the minimum energy.
:::

::: {.flow-arrow}
→
:::

::: {style="flex: 1; font-size: 0.75em;" .box}
**3. Identify muscle synergies**

Use matrix factorization to identify groups of muscles that activate together (temporally):

$$ \underbrace{M}_{\substack{\text{activation} \\ \text{matrix}}} \approx \overbrace{W}^{\llap{\substack{\text{temporal} \\ \text{activations}}\kern-1.5em}} \underbrace{H}_{\llap{\substack{\text{spatial} \\ \text{activations}}\kern-1.5em}}$$

and set the *synergies* as the output of the RL policy.
:::

::: {.flow-arrow}
→
:::

::: {style="flex: 1; font-size: 0.75em;" .box}
**4. Canonical RL**

With the synergy constraint baked in, optimize a composite reward function:

$$R = \mathbf{w}\begin{bmatrix}R_{\textrm{Velocity}} \\ R_{\textrm{Effort}} \\ R_{\textrm{R.o.M.}} \\ R_{\textrm{Fall}}\end{bmatrix}$$

Train across a variety of velocities and terrains.
:::
:::

# Bro
::: {.fragment}
**Two controllers, same everything else:**

- **Synergistic:** policy → 10 synergy weights per leg → $H$ → 40 muscles
- **Independent (baseline):** policy → every muscle directly

**Test:** compare both to treadmill data from 30 *other* people (22 + 8) [@camargo2021dataset; @scherpereel2023dataset]
:::

::: {.notes}
Steps 1 through 3 are just about building the synergies. They record one person walking, use a simulation (MocoInverse in OpenSim) to estimate what their muscles were doing, since there's no EMG, and then use NMF to find groups of muscles that tend to activate together. That gives 10 synergies per leg — that's the matrix H.

Step 4 is where RL comes in. Instead of the policy choosing 40 separate muscle activations per leg, it chooses how much of each of the 10 synergies to use, and H turns that into muscle activations. The reward only says "walk at this speed" — the human data is never used as a tracking target.

To see if this helps, they train a second controller that's identical except it sets every muscle directly. Then they compare both against treadmill data from 30 people who weren't used to build anything.
:::
